look_here_first: Start with the terminal spike and the narrow leaves. Texas stillingia is a many-stemmed perennial with linear serrate-glandular leaves, copious white latex, and a terminal inflorescence with pistillate flowers low on the axis and clusters of staminate flowers above.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial herb/subshrub with several to many stems from the base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves alternate, narrow linear, short-petiolate to nearly sessile

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf margins finely serrate with glandular teeth

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: pistillate flowers concentrated toward the base of the inflorescence

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: staminate flowers grouped above in condensed cymes

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Strong Euphorbiaceae teaching plant: latex plus highly reduced unisexual flowers and a male-above/female-below terminal inflorescence pattern.

key_traits.label: Video training
key_traits.text: Joey's frame shows the plant rooted directly among exposed Edwards Plateau limestone, reinforcing habitat recognition.
